findings.title: Breaking change to RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3
findings.body: The exit code for RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3, and the new FEATURE_DISABLED constant takes exit code 4. Any existing scripts or automation that were written against the previous exit code 4 to detect 'recreate upgrade needed' will now silently misinterpret the result (exit code 4 now means 'feature disabled'). Although this is a preview feature, the documentation in update-compatibility.adoc previously documented exit code 4 for the recreate case, so users who adopted the preview may have built automation around it. Consider whether a deprecation period or migration note is warranted.

findings.title: testFeatureNotEnabled only covers the metadata subcommand, not check
findings.body: The test `testFeatureNotEnabled` only verifies that the `metadata` subcommand fails when the feature is disabled. There is no corresponding test verifying that the `check` subcommand also correctly fails with exit code 4 and the appropriate error message when the feature is not enabled. Since both commands have identical feature-gate logic, a test for `check` would provide symmetric coverage.

findings.title: Feature not enabled when updateStrategy is null, potentially inconsistent with operator behavior
findings.body: When `updateStrategy` is null, `createInitialDeployment` returns early without enabling the `rolling-updates` feature. The documentation in advanced-configuration.adoc states 'While on preview stage, the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail.' If the operator enforces this check whenever it processes update logic (even for the default/null strategy path), this test case would fail at runtime. If the operator only requires the feature when `updateSpec` is explicitly set, the documentation should clarify this to avoid user confusion.
